Preparing Spatial Data

Divyashree Rana

2026-07-05

1 Load required packages

The following package is required for raster processing, moving window analyses, and exporting resistance surfaces for subsequent optimization.

library(terra)

2 Load 1 km raster surfaces

Environmental predictor rasters are first imported at their native 1 km resolution from Google Earth Engine and stored in ./input/rasters_1km. These rasters serve as the baseline inputs from which coarser-scale representations are generated using moving window smoothing. This allows rasters processed at different spatial scales to have same resolution and still mergeable for multisurface optimization.

2.1 Import raster layers

raster_dir <- "./input/rasters_1km"

files <- list.files(
  raster_dir,
  pattern = "\\.asc$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

files
## [1] "./input/rasters_1km/agri_dens_1km.asc"                      
## [2] "./input/rasters_1km/agri_dens_1km_1km.asc"                  
## [3] "./input/rasters_1km/dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km.asc"        
## [4] "./input/rasters_1km/dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km_1km.asc"    
## [5] "./input/rasters_1km/dist_water_30m_utm_1km.asc"             
## [6] "./input/rasters_1km/dist_water_30m_utm_1km_1km.asc"         
## [7] "./input/rasters_1km/MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km.asc"    
## [8] "./input/rasters_1km/MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km_1km.asc"
rasters <- rast(files)

rasters
## class       : SpatRaster 
## size        : 113, 169, 8  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
## resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
## extent      : 381000, 550000, 3074000, 3187000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
## coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 44N 
## sources     : agri_dens_1km.asc  
##               agri_dens_1km_1km.asc  
##               dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km.asc  
##               ... and 5 more sources
## names       : agri_~s_1km, agri_~s_1km, dist_~m_1km, dist_~m_1km, dist_~m_1km,  dist_~m_1km, ... 
## min values  :          ? ,           0,          ? ,    5.413951,          ? , 5.526969e-03, ... 
## max values  :          ? ,         100,          ? , 7772.756348,          ? , 1.462090e+04, ...

2.2 Check raster consistency

All raster layers should have identical extent, resolution, and coordinate reference system before moving window analyses are performed.

compareGeom(
  rasters[[1]],
  rasters[[2]]
)
## [1] TRUE
compareGeom(
  rasters[[1]],
  rasters[[3]]
)
## [1] TRUE
compareGeom(
  rasters[[1]],
  rasters[[4]]
)
## [1] TRUE

3 Generate smoothed raster surfaces

Moving window analyses are used to summarize environmental conditions across broader neighbourhoods while maintaining the original 1 km raster resolution. Circular moving windows with radii of 2 km, 5 km, and 10 km are applied using focal means.

3.1 Define moving windows

w2 <- focalMat(
  rasters[[1]],
  d = 2000,
  type = "circle"
)

w5 <- focalMat(
  rasters[[1]],
  d = 5000,
  type = "circle"
)

w10 <- focalMat(
  rasters[[1]],
  d = 10000,
  type = "circle"
)

3.2 Applying moving window smoothening to the 1km rasters

rasters_2km <- focal(
  rasters,
  w = w2,
  fun = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

rasters_5km <- focal(
  rasters,
  w = w5,
  fun = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

rasters_10km <- focal(
  rasters,
  w = w10,
  fun = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

3.3 Verify smoothed rasters

Moving window smoothing should preserve raster geometry and should not introduce missing values along raster edges.

compareGeom(
  rasters,
  rasters_2km
)
## [1] TRUE
compareGeom(
  rasters,
  rasters_5km
)
## [1] TRUE
compareGeom(
  rasters,
  rasters_10km
)
## [1] TRUE
global(
  rasters_2km,
  fun = function(x) sum(is.na(x))
)
##                                   global

## dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km.1          0

## dist_water_30m_utm_1km.1               0
## MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km        0
## MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km.1      0
global(
  rasters_5km,
  fun = function(x) sum(is.na(x))
)
##                                   global

## dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km            0
## dist_settlement_10m_utm_1km.1          0
## dist_water_30m_utm_1km                 0
## dist_water_30m_utm_1km.1               0
## MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km        0
## MODIS_EVI_rescaled_500m_utm_1km.1      0
global(
  rasters_10km,
  fun = function(x) sum(is.na(x))
)

3.4 Visualize smoothed raster surfaces

par(mfrow = c(2,2), mar = c(2,2,2,4))

plot(
  rasters,
  main = paste(names(rasters), "\n1 km")
)

plot(
  rasters_2km,
  main = paste(names(rasters_2km), "\n2 km")
)

plot(
  rasters_5km,
  main = paste(names(rasters_5km), "\n5 km")
)

plot(
  rasters_10km,
  main = paste(names(rasters_10km), "\n10 km")
)

par(mfrow = c(1,1))

4 Export raster surfaces

Raster stacks from each spatial scale are exported as ASCII grids for use in subsequent resistance surface optimization analyses. Create a ./input/smooth folder for storing these processed layers of at multiple scales all with a resolution of 1km.

raster_list <- list(
  "1km" = rasters,
  "2km" = rasters_2km,
  "5km" = rasters_5km,
  "10km" = rasters_10km
)

base_dir <- "./input/smooth"

for(scale_name in names(raster_list)) {

  r_stack <- raster_list[[scale_name]]

  out_dir <- file.path(
    base_dir,
    paste0("rasters_", scale_name)
  )
  
  ## Create output directory if it does not already exist
  if(!dir.exists(out_dir)){

    dir.create(
      out_dir,
      recursive = TRUE,
      showWarnings = FALSE
    )

  }

  for(i in 1:nlyr(r_stack)) {

    writeRaster(

      r_stack[[i]],

      filename = file.path(
        out_dir,
        paste0(
          names(r_stack)[i],
          "_",
          scale_name,
          ".asc"
        )
      ),

      overwrite = TRUE,

      filetype = "AAIGrid"

    )

  }

}
